title: Signal eddy — priority catalog & probe hypotheses
content:
Purpose: quick-working synthesis of recent customer threads (Apr–Jun 2026) that have been circulating — an "signal eddy" — where the same asks keep recirculating across accounts. Goal: produce a small prioritized catalog and a slate of fast probes (micro-experiments and docs) we can ship in 1–4 sprints to reduce noise and gather leading indicators for larger product work.

Method & sources:
- Inputs: 18 CS threads, 6 technical support cases, 3 enterprise sales discovery calls, two post-mortems on tail latency incidents, and a set of slack threads (#dedicated-latency, #optimize-feedback).
- Lightweight clustering: grouped asks by operational impact (latency/cost/observability/UX) and by workload archetype (real-time chat, batch re-ranking, embedding-heavy search).
- Bias note: heavy weight on enterprise customers using Dedicated and Private deployments; smaller accounts show up as representative edge cases.

High-level takeaway (one line):
There are three persistent eddies: (A) tail-latency / KV-cache fragility, (B) cost-uncertainty for mixed workloads (embeddings + gen), and (C) rollout opacity & model mismatch risk. Each is driving repeated feature asks that we can address with a mix of runtime patches, docs, and telemetry probes.

Signal eddy clusters (digest):
1) Tail-latency & KV cache fragility (Eddy A)
- Symptom: intermittent long tails on warm requests (300–1200ms above SLO) for chat workloads when context sizes jump > 1k tokens.
- Customer quotes: "We see a >3x latency spike when a handful of users have long histories; it kills our SLOs and billing metrics." —Large FinTech account
- Frequent asks: more deterministic KV-cache eviction, better visibility into per-request cache hits, option to pin prefix caches for high-value sessions.
- Risk if unaddressed: customer fallback to simpler stateless routing or keeping smaller conversation windows, which reduces product value.
- Quick probe(s):
  * Instrumentation probe: add per-request KV cache hit/miss counters into Console trace and a light-weight sample payload (first draft dashboard mock in linked confluence). Owner: Jamal. Delivery: 1 sprint.
  * Runtime micropatch: configurable sticky prefix cache (config flag: runtime.cache.pin_prefix_seconds) with default off. Fast opt-in for Dedicated customers. Owner: Ethan. Delivery: 2 sprints (QA on Dedicated).

2) Cost uncertainty for mixed workloads (Eddy B)
- Symptom: customers running embedding-heavy indexing alongside gen routes can't predict per-session unit economics; batching/caching suggestions are generic and not workload-aware.
- Customer quotes: "Our embedding jobs blow up cost on some days; we need better cost signals before we commit Reserved capacity." —Mid-market search vendor
- Frequent asks: per-route cost forecasting, simulated billing for hypothetical batching/quantization changes, and clearer guidance on when Dedicated/Private reduces unit cost vs hosted.
- Quick probe(s):
  * Cost-simulation microtool: a tiny web UI (or console beta) where customers paste traffic mix (e.g., 70% embeddings, 30% gen) and see estimated cost delta for different batch sizes / quantization. Integrate with usage sampling. Owner: Priya. Delivery: 3 sprints (MVP).
  * Prominent docs: short playbook "when to choose Dedicated vs Hosted for embedding-heavy workloads" — include 3 worked examples. Owner: Ava. Delivery: 1 sprint.

3) Rollout opacity & model mismatch (Eddy C)
- Symptom: customers are concerned about silent quality regressions during model upgrades and fallback routing. They want per-traffic-model canaries, clearer rollback diagnostics, and better prompt-set level regression alerts.
- Customer quotes: "We can't tell if the spike in hallucinations came from the new variant or config changes — we need a simple signal." —Enterprise analytics platform
- Frequent asks: prompt-set eval hooks, canary percent controls by route, and auto-rollback triggers tied to quality metrics.
- Quick probe(s):
  * Canary control button in Console: simple slider to split 0–10% traffic, with synthetic prompt-set eval baked in and a required manual confirmation for >10%. Owner: Product Console team (ask: console eng to prototype). Delivery: 2 sprints for alpha.
  * Prompt-set regression alerting: integrate a small evaluation runner that scores a curated prompt set daily and notifies customers if A-B difference exceeds threshold. Owner: Priya + Applied ML. Delivery: 3 sprints (alpha).

Prioritization rationale (short):
- A (Tail-latency) has immediate revenue and SLA risk for large accounts — high impact, medium effort.
- B (Cost-sim) reduces churn risk at the reservation decision point — medium impact, low-to-medium effort (docs + tool).
- C (Rollout visibility) is lower immediate revenue risk but high strategic value (trust) — medium impact, medium effort.

Micro-ship plan (1–4 sprints):
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): KV-cache instrumentation dashboard (A-instrumentation), Dedicated prefix pin flag spec, and the Dedicated vs Hosted playbook doc (B-doc).
- Sprint 2: implement runtime sticky prefix (A-patch) behind a gate for Dedicated, Console slider alpha for canaries (C-alpha).
- Sprint 3: cost-simulation MVP (B-tool) + prompt-set runner alpha (C-eval). Publish a short release note and customer-facing FAQ for the three items.

Representative tickets & customers to loop in:
- RED-1023 (Sales discovery thread, FinTech latency SLA) — linked above
- ENG-erv-431 (tail-latency sample tracer work) — recommend tagging for Jamal/Ethan pairing
- CS-Case-8742 (embedding billing spike) — contact: Maya Patel, customer lead

Open questions & risk notes (scratch):
- Sticky prefix pinning: risk that pinned prefixes increase memory pressure on nodes. Need SRE capacity estimate and a quota guard (per-tenant pin budget). (TODO: SRE cost estimate).
- Cost-sim tooling: requires sampled token counts which may raise privacy questions for Private deployments — design for opt-in telemetry or synthetic sampling.
- Prompt-set evals: maintenance cost of keeping representative prompt sets; need an onboarding flow for customers to adopt/own their suites. Could we seed with a small Redwood curated set?

Communication plan for customers:
- Draft a single-page FAQ for CS to use in responses (one-liner fixes + links to console beta).
- Host a 30-min office hours slot with top-10 Dedicated customers to demo sticky-prefix and canary slider when alpha ready.

Next steps (who does what):
1) Jamal: instrument KV cache traces + mock dashboard tiles — due 2026-06-29.
2) Ava: publish Dedicated vs Hosted playbook doc draft and customer examples — due 2026-06-22.
3) Ethan: spike on sticky prefix runtime flag and collab with SRE for memory/budget model — spike due 2026-06-30.
4) Priya: cost-sim wireframe + gather sample traffic mixes from 3 pilot customers — wireframe due 2026-07-02.

Notes to self / low-priority ideas (keep as parking lot):
- Consider an "embeddings thermostat" that automatically delays embedding batch jobs into off-peak windows to smooth billing spikes (more of a scheduling product).
- Explore a short-runner A/B test where we expose per-session estimated bill after 10 sessions — will this change user behavior?

Slack & comms anchors: see #dedicated-latency (primer thread: slack thread ts 16234567), #optimize-betas (signup list), and the confluence page in linked_artifacts for dashboard mocks.

Summary (TL;DR): focus first on making tail-latency visible and tractable (small instrumentation + sticky-prefix opt-in). Pair that with a concise Dedicated-vs-Hosted playbook and a cost-simulation MVP to reduce churn at the reservation decision. Canary tooling and prompt-set evals are next-level trust bets.

-- end of working draft --
